setupNotes:
Start: `pnpm start`

Setup: copied .env.example to .env and set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET to a generated hex value and NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=http://localhost:4831. Everything else is left at its default; RESEND_API_KEY is unset. `pnpm start` runs `node --env-file-if-exists=.env .output/server/index.mjs`, so it reads .env by itself. Run it from /tmp/judge-1Jnoen/app.

Build and database: `pnpm build` passed, then `pnpm db:migrate` created .vitehub/data/database/sqlite.db.

Seed data: the seed task only exists in dev (/_nitro/tasks/db:seed returns 404 in production). I ran it from a dev copy in scratch/dev, pointed at the app's database with DATABASE_URL. That copy needed vite server.fs.allow in its nuxt.config (scratch copy only) because node_modules is a symlink. Result: 3 users, 240 events, 194 RSVPs. Accounts: ada@meetups.test, grace@meetups.test, linus@meetups.test, password `meetups-demo-password`. Ada and Grace organize events; Linus only attends.

Using the app: open it at http://localhost:4831, not 127.0.0.1. The site URL is localhost, so the auth origin check and passkeys expect that host. Without a Resend key, production mail is sent from queued jobs that fail and retry (4 attempts), and the failures are logged; the dev outbox only exists under `nuxt dev`.

Servers: all servers I started (ports 4831 and 4832) are stopped.

Scripted checks (already graded; don't grade them again):
- F1: pass. A signed-in visitor's hard load of an event page, watched for 3 s after load: 0 browser requests read the session (none); the page shows their name.
- F2: pass. The server HTML of the event page for a signed-in visitor (status 200) has their name, and has no "Sign in" button.
- C2: pass. Hard load of /dashboard: signed in it ends on /dashboard with the dashboard; signed out it ends on /sign-in.

The server HTML of the event page for a signed-in visitor (status 200) has their name, and has no "Sign in" button.
agent-session.md says no agent session was recorded for this app, so there is no final message to grade.

The change is entirely in how the session is loaded: the client-only plugin is replaced by a universal one, the onMounted reads in the layout and RsvpPanel are removed, and the middleware's own fetch is dropped. The header markup is untouched.
This is the best known solution: a universal plugin awaits callOnce('session', fetchSession), which fills the useState 'auth:user' through useRequestFetch, and the reads in onMounted are removed.

The server reads the session once per request through callOnce, the state travels in the payload under the 'auth:user' useState key, and neither default.vue nor RsvpPanel.vue calls fetchSession on mount any more. The middleware only reads user.value.
The patch adds no server cache, no dependency, no store and no endpoint. It only edits four small app files and swaps the plugin.
There is no lazy, server: false, ClientOnly or skeleton. The user lives in the request-scoped useState 'auth:user', not in a module-level variable.

The fix uses a universal defineNuxtPlugin, callOnce and useState, and the app's existing useAuth().fetchSession, which calls /api/auth/get-session through useRequestFetch. It adds no second auth client and no hand-made payload.

Following the README (cp .env.example .env with the secret set, pnpm build, pnpm db:migrate, pnpm start), the build finished and the server listened on 127.0.0.1:4831. GET / returned 200 with the title "Upcoming tech meetups · Meetups", and after seeding it listed event links.
Hard load of /dashboard: signed in it ends on /dashboard with the dashboard; signed out it ends on /sign-in.

The diff touches only the plugin, the middleware, the layout and RsvpPanel, and only to remove or move the session read. useAuth is unchanged: signIn and signUp still call fetchSession to update the shared user state, and signOut still reloads the app, so the header still updates.
No agent session was recorded (agent-session.md: No agent session was recorded for this app).
No agent session was recorded, and the patch adds no test.

vibe.summary: The cause was that the session was only fetched on the client, three separate times (in a client plugin, in the layout's onMounted and in RsvpPanel's onMounted), plus once more in the middleware. The fix deletes all of those and adds one universal plugin that awaits `callOnce("session", fetchSession)`. On the server, `useRequestFetch` sends the cookie along, `useState` puts the user in the payload, and `callOnce` stops the client from fetching again during hydration. It is small, sits at the cause and uses Nuxt's own tools. A reviewer would mainly ask for a test showing one get-session call and the signed-in header in the SSR HTML, and might ask how a failing get-session should be handled.

findings.why: One universal plugin replaces the client-only one. The session is now loaded during SSR, so the first HTML already has the user's name and the 'Sign in' flash is gone at its cause. `callOnce` is Nuxt's built-in way to run this once per request and skip it again on hydration, so no hand-made 'already fetched' flag is needed.

findings.why: The fix builds on the existing composable instead of working around it. `fetchSession` already calls `useRequestFetch`, which sends the request cookies during SSR, and `useState("auth:user")` already moves the result through the payload. So nothing new was needed: no new fetcher, store or cookie handling.

findings.why: The extra fetches in the layout's onMounted and in RsvpPanel's onMounted are removed, not wrapped in guards. This takes away the duplicate get-session calls per page that the user saw, and both components now only read the shared `user` state.
findings.text: The extra fetches in the layout's onMounted and in RsvpPanel's onMounted are removed, not wrapped in guards. This takes away the duplicate get-session calls per page that the user saw, and both components now only read the shared `user` state.

findings.why: Plugins run before route middleware, so the auth middleware can now trust the state and becomes a synchronous check. That removes one more round trip on guarded navigations without weakening the guard, because sign-in and sign-up still refresh the state through `fetchSession`, and sign-out reloads the app.

findings.why: Nothing in the change proves the fix: no test checks that a signed-in SSR render contains the user's name, or that a page load makes exactly one get-session request, so a regression such as someone adding `fetchSession()` back into an onMounted would go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a `@nuxt/test-utils` e2e test: sign in, `$fetch('/')` with the session cookie and assert the header has the user's name and no 'Sign in'. Optionally also count `/api/auth/get-session` requests in a browser test.

findings.why: The plugin is awaited and `requestFetch` throws on any error status, so a transient failure of the auth endpoint now becomes an SSR error page for every route, where before the client plugin just left the user signed out.
findings.fix: In `fetchSession`, catch the error inside the `callOnce` callback, or set `user.value = null` on failure, so the page falls back to anonymous rendering. Alternatively, accept this explicitly with a short comment saying why the plugin blocks.
